Aerial Wildlife 
Survey Report 
WMU 544 Aerial Ungulate Survey – February 2018 
 
Background 
Wildlife Management Unit (WMU) 544, “Utikuma Lake”, covers an area of 7,177 km 2 and is located north of 
Lesser Slave Lake, Alberta. The WMU is bounded to the south by the southern shore of Les ser Slave Lake, to the 
east by Highway 88, and to the north by the Seal Lake Road. The WMU boundary extends west along the 
southern lakeshore to Highway 750, then north to the northern boundary of Township 77, then west again to the 
ATCO Electric transmission line 7L11, where it runs north to the Seal Lake Road.  
 
The most recent moose (Alces alces) survey in WMU 544 was completed in 2011 using the stratified random 
block method (Table 1). Estimated population density was 0.28 moose/km 2 (90% CI 0.24 – 0.32; CV = 0.095), 
and estimated population size was 1568 moose (1329 – 1806). The age-sex composition ratio (bull:cow:calf) 
based on moose observed within survey units in 2011 was 39:100:49. 
 
The objective of this distance survey was to estimate total population sizes, population densities, and age -sex 
composition ratios of moose in WMU 544 to inform game management decisions.  
Methods 
An aerial ungulate survey was conducted in WMU 544 from February 10 to 12, 2018, using the distance sampling 
method (Buckland et al. 2001). A total of 176 parallel north-south transect lines (survey effort = 1192.8 km; 
interval = 1.2 km) were flown with a Bell 206 Jet Ranger over three consecutive days. Data were analyzed using 
the program “Distance” (Version 6.0, Release 2; Thomas et al. 2010).  
Results 
A total of 107 moose were observed in 76 groups. Of these, 23 (21.5%) were bulls, 55 (51.4%) were cows, 26 
(24.3%) were calves, and 3 (2.8%) were unclassified, which yielded an age-sex composition ratio (bull:cow:calf) 
of 42:100:47. The final estimated moose density in WMU 544 was 0.117 moose/km2 (90% CI 0.094 – 0.146), and 
estimated abundance was 673 moose (90% CI 540 – 839; Table 1).
